messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: interesting paper on model selection
parts:
Dear all,

I quite liked this paper on model selection: Tredennick, A. T., G. Hooker, S. P. Ellner, and P. B. Adler. 2021. A practical guide to selecting models for exploration, inference, and prediction in ecology. Ecology 102(6):e03336. 10.1002/ecy.3336

I had always been wondering how one can choose a model if we are not going to first state the objective of the modeling. These authors argue that very different strategies of model selection may be appropriate depending on whether the goal of your model building is data exploration, inference (= mechanisms), or prediction. If you recognize this then you're perhaps less likely to get lost in the Black Hole of statistics.

Best regards --- Marc

parts:
Hi,

I quite liked reading this article too, thanks for sharing. It definitely can help me improve the way I choose and fit models.

I came to wonder, am I right in thinking that a GoF is not an out-of-sample cross-validation? Rather sort of a "within-sample" one. 
Is there any out-of-sample cross-validation technic tailored for typical Unmarked models (output from Occu or Colext for example) ?

Best regards,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: interesting paper on model selection
parts:
Salut Vincent,

I don't think there is any for models fit in unmarked, but for the models that can be fit using (under the hood) STAN in the sister package ubms, there is a leave-one-out cross-validation score that is automatically computed for every model fit.

Best regards  --- Marc
